explanations: The liveness handler runs the Postgres probe and returns 503 when it fails. Liveness failures make the orchestrator restart the container, so a database blip or failover restarts every replica at once even though the processes are healthy; on restart they all reconnect and rerun the migration step together, which can prolong the outage. Dependency health belongs only in readiness (which already checks Postgres); liveness should only confirm the process itself can respond.

The router is mounted and the server listens before migrations run. readiness checks !state.migrationsApplied first and returns 503 with status 'starting' before calling runAll. 'draining' only applies after SIGTERM.

ehrGatewayProbe throws on a non-ok response; runAll uses Promise.allSettled and maps the rejection into ok: false with the message. Since not every outcome is ok, the handler returns 503 'not_ready'. The throw never escapes, so there is no 500.

The SIGTERM handler sets state.draining, so readiness returns 503 'draining' immediately, giving the load balancer time to stop routing. After 10_000 ms it calls server.close, and in its callback ends the pool and exits.
